note: Candidate learning store (safe-versioning rules 6-7, docs/15). New corrections/rules enter HERE first and do NOT modify global production rules. A candidate is promoted into config/QUALITY_MEMORY.json (validated) only after it improves an output or gets explicit user approval. A candidate that causes worse results is set status=disabled with its failure evidence — kept, never deleted, so it is not repeated. Both pipeline versions may read this; rolling back code never touches it.

schema.observation: what was seen / the proposed rule
schema.evidence: SKU / image / correction that motivated it
schema.disabled_reason: why it was turned off (when disabled) — evidence retained

candidates.observation: composite-v1 from 2D CAD renders can guarantee geometry for STUDIO/product shots at the angles the CAD provides (ring composited into a clean cloth scene = source pixels, all geometry/head/invention checks pass). It CANNOT reliably produce WORN LIFESTYLE / close-up shots: a top-down CAD ring composited onto an angled finger looks pasted (fails natural integration + correct-scale-on-hand). Worn geometry-perfect shots need FALLBACK 2 (render the worn angle from a 3D CAD model, docs/13 §6) or a real worn photograph (e.g. LR-0151 'Model G' is a real worn photo of the actual ring). Therefore a COMPLETE 12-image catalog (incl. 4 lifestyle + 3 closeup) cannot pass the full acceptance criteria from 2D CAD alone.
candidates.evidence: LR-0151 proof: studio composite passed all 21 geometry/head/invention checks; the earlier worn-composite attempt + the angle mismatch show lifestyle is the gap. Composite integrity also requires a clean ring-free scene (composite-integrity fix).
